entries.title: I use technology to give students a voice and become critical digital citizens.
entries.summary: Empower students using Google Sites, Gemini, and Vids to build critical thinking skills. See how these tools help kids find their voice today.
entries.content:
Technology in the classroom is not about replacing teachers — it’s about giving students room to unlock their curiosity and take ownership of their learning. In my daily teaching, I use Google Sites, Gemini Notebook, and Google Vids to help my students move from just consuming information to creating something of their own.

I design collaborative Sites where my students share what they learn to deeply strengthen analytical skills. They work through self-paced study notebooks, and use Vids to turn their ideas into creative video presentations.

For me, my focus is about giving every child an equal chance to collaborate, think critically, and find their voice. On World Teachers' Day, we celebrate the incredible magic that happens when great teaching meets helpful technology to help build confident, capable kids ready for the future.

entries.title: Technology helps my students balance big creative ideas with tight deadlines.
entries.summary: Students use Google Drive for video assets and Sheets for production timelines to meet tight deadlines. See how these tools boost classroom output.
entries.content:
Teaching Media Production, Media Print, and Business Writing is rewarding, but balancing technical training with creative energy can be a challenge.

Every day, technology helps me keep our fast-paced classroom organized. My students rely on Google Drive to store large video assets, swap high-resolution photos, and give real-time feedback on each other's work. To keep our ambitious broadcast schedules and yearbook print deadlines on track, we use Google Sheets to assign tasks and manage production timelines. It has enhanced our ability to provide quality production pieces, while ensuring the work is productive and organized.

These simple collaborative tools keep our classroom running smoothly, giving my students the structure they need to build technical confidence, work as a team, and bring their creative ideas to life.

Michelle, second from left, and her colleagues

entries.title: Here’s how I use technology to bring science to life in my classroom.
entries.summary: See how this teacher uses Gemini and Gemini Notebook to build digital literacy and refine lesson plans. Read the full story to improve your teaching.
entries.content:
Walking into my 8th-grade science classroom each morning is a surreal experience. I am teaching in the exact room where I sat as a middle schooler. Coming full circle after 17 years across education has taught me that great teaching starts with staying a curious learner alongside my students.

Today, my students do not learn through static lectures. We run interactive simulations where they can discover scientific patterns firsthand. In my own planning, I lean on Gemini to review unit plans against standards and brainstorm new approaches. By openly modeling tools like Gemini and Gemini Notebook, my students have built real digital literacy.

Technology never replaces our heart in the classroom; it just gives us more room to connect and inspire.

entries.title: World Teachers’ Day 2026
entries.summary: To celebrate World Teachers’ Day 2026, educators share their stories about how they use tech in the classroom.
entries.content:
This World Teachers’ Day, we’re celebrating the voices and stories of educators around the world.

We asked teachers to share in their own words how they navigate everyday challenges and bring new learning experiences to life. These educators are thoughtfully using technology to help their students understand complex concepts, create engaging lessons, and support critical thinking. At Google, we design our educational tools in partnership with teachers and focus on keeping them at the heart of learning. No technology can replace the role that a teacher plays in the life of their students, mentoring and inspiring them to reach their full potential.

To help elevate teacher stories, like the ones in this World Teachers’ Day collection, we’re partnering with TED to launch a global idea search for educators who are innovating with technology. As teaching and learning continue to evolve, we believe that educator insights, ideas, and visions for the future of education should be leading the way. Educators with the most compelling ideas will have the chance to share their talks from the TED stage.

Explore the stories below to hear directly from educators and learn how you can share your ideas with TED and Google by registering for the Idea Workshop.

entries.title: I teach my students that in the AI era, critical thinking comes first.
entries.summary: A California teacher uses Gemini to streamline lesson planning in Google Drive. See how she prioritizes critical thinking in the AI era.
entries.content:
When I started teaching 25 years ago in India, classroom technology meant learning basic computer navigation. Today, as a middle school technology teacher in California, the landscape looks very different.

Today, Gemini helps me tackle lesson planning and differentiated instruction in a fraction of the time, keeping my prep secure in Google Drive.

For my middle schoolers, seeing AI in action helps remove the fear of the unknown. I always remind them: AI only mirrors human design. Real power comes from our ability to reason, question, and keep our own critical thinking first.

entries.title: My eighth-grade students built our school newscast from scratch with Gemini.
entries.summary: Eighth graders built The Cougar Rumble newscast using Gemini and Google Docs. See how these students streamlined their production workflow today.
entries.content:
When my 8th-grade students decided to launch our school’s first-ever newscast, we started from scratch: no name, no logo, and no established brand. By using Gemini as a creative partner alongside Google Docs and Slides, my students built our show, “The Cougar Rumble,” from the ground up.

Students collaborated on initial concepts, used Gemini to identify the common themes across their logo sketches, and generated prompts to refine their brand kit. Today, that same workflow powers our weekly broadcasts, helping teams polish scripts and organize shot lists before filming. Rather than replacing their creativity, tools like Gemini give my students more opportunities to brainstorm, revise, and bring their original ideas to life.

entries.title: My students use Gemini to brainstorm creative ideas.
entries.summary: Fifth graders use Google Gemini to write songs about history and create art. See how this teacher integrates AI into the classroom.
entries.content:
For nearly three decades, I’ve explored how classroom technology can help students find their voice. When generative AI arrived, I wanted my fifth graders to understand how to guide these tools thoughtfully, even without direct access.

Using a simple Google Forms setup, my students write and refine prompts that I run through Google Gemini on their behalf. In our art and values project, one student used descriptive prompting to create an image representing school values, bringing an idea to life that he previously lacked the drawing tools to express. During history, students used Gemini to compose original songs about Westward Expansion, fact-checking and editing lyrics along the way.

By treating Gemini as a brainstorming partner, my students are learning that technology works best when human creativity leads the way.

entries.title: Technology is helping my fellow math teachers trade weekend prep for personalized learning.
entries.summary: Teachers use Gemini to build custom K-6 math worksheets and save hours of prep time. See how Google AI transforms classroom instruction.
entries.content:
In primary school mathematics, the challenge isn’t a lack of resources, it’s a lack of relevant ones. Teachers spend hours searching for activities aligned to specific lesson timing, often sacrificing weekends to build materials from scratch.

As an Education Officer, I set out to give teachers their time back while improving classroom learning. Using Gemini, I built custom interactive math challenges and customizable K-6 worksheets tailored precisely to our syllabus. I organized these on a Google Site into three levels of difficulty to differentiate instruction on the spot.

The impact has been immediate: students consolidate concepts right away, while teachers save hours of prep time. Next we’re training our leaders and teachers to build their own interactives. It’s no longer about searching endlessly online for the right activity, it’s about having the AI capability to create exactly what your students need in seconds.

entries.title: Gemini helps me bring hands-on learning into the classroom.
entries.summary: A teacher uses Google Gemini to design interactive role-playing simulations and nutrition lessons. See how AI boosts classroom engagement.
entries.content:
Before using AI, I often struggled to bridge the gap between abstract literature concepts and true hands-on learning. Today, Gemini serves as my planning partner, helping me build classroom experiences I couldn’t have easily created on my own a few years ago.

In my English classes, before we read complex stories about climate change or human rights, my students participate in global simulations. Gemini helps me quickly build multi-station role-playing challenges, letting students physically move through the room to solve problems and build empathy before opening their books. In my Life Skills courses, Gemini helps me design smoothie recipes and dietary profiles so students can blend ingredients and practice mindful nutrition firsthand.

Gemini isn’t a replacement for active teaching — it’s a tool that helps me bring movement and deeper engagement into my classroom.

entries.title: I replaced traditional coding tests with real conversations about how my students solve problems using AI.
entries.summary: Replace coding tests with AI-driven interviews using Google Gemini in Colab. See how this professor evaluates student judgment. Read the full report.
entries.content:
Embedding AI as a collaborative thinking partner completely transformed how I assess my data mining students.

Instead of spending hours grinding through coding syntax, they use Gemini in Google Colab as a personal tutor. While the AI suggests code and alternatives, students must decide what to use, question the suggestions, and justify final modelling decisions.

This creates a meaningful form of human–AI teaming. Because AI can increasingly produce a working model, what matters is whether students can exercise judgment over the AI supporting them. I conduct verbal interviews where students defend their choices, troubleshoot and identify where AI's recommendations may be incorrect. Behind the scenes, Gemini Canvas and Gemini Notebook help me evaluate this work at scale.

Balancing my roles as a professor and Chief Digital Officer, my core belief remains: we aren't replacing learning with AI, but intentionally redesigning it to build lasting human capability rather than tech dependency.
